newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps firm - Mogas up $2, CFDs climb again.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps firm - Mogas up $2, CFDs climb again.

text.p: European oil swaps firmed again on Tuesday, buoyed by firm Brent crude futures and healthy refinery margins in Europe.
Brent crude CFDs rose about four cents for this week to 38 cents under June. This compares with levels of around 63 cents under a week ago.
The next three weeks also edged higher to 39 cents, 34 cents and 32 cents under respectively.
Gasoline swaps rose $2 a tonne, supported by big gains in the U.S. on Monday.
Rotterdam barges traded up to $195.50 for early May with swaps heard in the range $199 to $199.50 by lunchtime. June talked some $3.50 a tonne lower with July a further $3.50 below June.
Naphtha gained a similar amount to talk around $183 for May and $185 for June and July.

Heavy fuel firmed $2 a tonne to talk around $85 for May barges after demand from Portugal for up to three cargoes of fuel was reported on Monday. June was $1.50 higher but dealers said the thin physical market had dampened trade. Low sulphur was valued just above $90 for May.
Gas oil against Brent held at $4.35 a barrel on the third quarter and $4.85 on the fourth.

Jet premiums were flat with May bid at $24.50 a tonne above the IPE after trading at that level last Thursday. The third and fourth quarters were little changed at $27.50 and $31.50 above the screen respectively.
